literal: Hair if removed not-living kavari-animal those-who-are-like, life they-will-remove honor if-comes.
translation: Those who are like the kavari animal, which cannot live if it loses its hair, will give up their lives if an affront to their honor comes.
modern: தன் உடலிலிருந்து மயிர் நீங்கினால் உயிர் வாழாத கவரிமானைப் போன்றவர்கள், தங்கள் மானத்திற்கு ஒரு குறை வந்தால் உயிரையே விட்டுவிடுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares honorable people to the legendary kavari animal (often identified as the yak), which is said to die if it loses its hair. The word 'kavarimā' denotes this specific animal, while 'vāḻā' emphasizes its inability to survive the loss of its defining feature. Similarly, for people of true honor, their dignity is as vital as life itself. If a situation arises where their honor is compromised ('māṉam variṉ'), they will readily give up their life ('uyir nīppar') rather than live in disgrace.
